observations: Photo 0 and 1 show a dirty V8 engine with intake manifold, valve covers, and extensive wiring harness attached to a transmission case at the bottom.
Photo 2 shows the transmission/bellhousing end close up, with hoses and connectors still attached, resting on bare ground next to a person's leg for scale.
A blue strap is wrapped around the midsection of the assembly, likely for handling or hoisting.
The items sit outdoors on wood pallets/ground in what looks like a used-parts yard, with other engines and transmissions visible in the background.
No part number, casting mark, Ford logo, or model tag is legible in any photo.
A 'GEARUP INC.' watermark appears on all three photos; this is a marketing/reseller mark, not proof of origin or fitment.
The assembly includes a full engine, not just a standalone gearbox, despite the listing title calling it a 'Gearbox'.

identity.kind: used engine and automatic transmission (gearbox) assembly, V8, for a full-size van

claims.claim: American drive Gearbox for Ford Econoline E150 E250 E350 V8
claims.evidence: No Ford casting marks, VIN tag, or part number are visible in photo 0, 1, or 2 to confirm make, model, or fitment.
Origin/import status cannot be confirmed from photos; no customs sticker, paperwork, or distinguishing tokunbo marking is shown.

risks.risk: Transmission may not actually fit the stated Econoline E150/E250/E350 models since no part number or tag is visible.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the casting number or tag stamped on the transmission case or bellhousing.
risks.if_unproven: priced as an unconfirmed-fitment used transmission, not as a guaranteed Econoline-specific part

risks.risk: Mechanical condition and whether the gearbox shifts, holds gears, or has internal damage cannot be judged from static photos.
risks.proof: A video of the transmission being turned over by hand/input shaft rotating smoothly, or a bench/engine-running test clip.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / functional condition unknown

risks.risk: Heavy dirt, dried mud, and debris coating the case may be hiding cracks, weld repairs, or casing damage.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the cleaned case surfaces, especially the bellhousing and mounting ears.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming possible hidden case damage

risks.risk: Listing says 'Gearbox' but photos show a full engine attached; unclear if buyer is paying for engine+transmission or transmission alone, and whether the engine runs.
risks.proof: Seller confirmation in writing plus a photo of the engine and transmission separated, or a running video of the engine.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a non-running engine bundled with an unverified-condition transmission, not as a standalone tested gearbox

risks.risk: Wiring harness and sensors look fatigued/worn (photo 0, 1); some connectors look clipped or stripped, which could affect electronic/automatic transmission control.
risks.proof: Close-up of the wiring harness connectors and the transmission control module/plug.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming harness and sensors need replacement

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of any stamped part number, casting number, or Ford tag on the transmission case or bellhousing.
Video of the input/output shaft being rotated by hand to show the gearbox is not seized.
Clarification and photo showing whether the engine and transmission are sold together or the transmission alone.
Photo of the transmission pan, fluid condition, and any visible leaks once wiped down.
response.reason: The assembly is identifiable by type as a used V8 engine-and-transmission unit, but no model tag or part number is visible to confirm the claimed Ford Econoline fitment, and no proof of function is given, so it must be priced at worst case as an unverified-fitment, untested used transmission bundled with a non-confirmed-running engine.
